summary.headline: Laser Power Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 2% YoY to INR628 crore, with EBITDA margin at 12.1% and PAT of INR31 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue from operations was about INR628 crore, up 2.1% YoY and 20.5% QoQ, driven by manufacturing (INR524 crore, up 29.9% YoY) while EPC fell to INR104 crore from INR212 crore on heavy-rain execution delays. EBITDA was INR76 crore (12.1% margin vs 13% a year earlier) and PAT was INR31 crore, up 44% QoQ. Management highlighted entry into high-voltage transmission via a first commercial HTLS order from Power Grid (INR72.76 crore) and a first 220 kV underground EPC order from CESC (about INR42-44 crore). Working capital rose to INR1,159 crore, with days at 166, and borrowings were cut to about INR499 crore after IPO-funded repayment of about INR490 crore.

segments.name: Manufacturing (cables, conductors)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR524 crore, up 29.9% YoY; H1 revenue INR906 crore, up 13.8% YoY. Management cites manufacturing margins of roughly 10-11%.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR104 crore vs INR212 crore a year earlier; H1 INR243 crore, down 10.7% YoY. Management says about INR100 crore of EPC revenue was deferred by monsoon-related delays and expects recovery in Q2-Q3, with EPC margins of about 14-16%.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to stabilise in the 12.5%-13% range for H2 and the full year.

H1 typically delivers 40-42% of full-year revenue; an analyst's implied FY27 revenue of about INR2,700 crore was not disputed, and FY27 EBITDA was not confirmed at INR340 crore, though management reiterated the 12.5-13% margin range.
Interest savings from IPO-funded debt repayment expected to reflect more fully in H2, supporting PAT margin improvement.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive for FY27.
Working capital days targeted to fall by 25-40 days by Q4 FY27.
Planned order inflow to keep improving by year-end; no firm order-inflow figure given.
capex_capacity: Kharagpur: provisional LoI and in-principle approval from WBIDC for about 40 acres at Vidyasagar Industrial Park on long-term lease, for an integrated power cable and conductor plant.
Management says the Kharagpur land is adjacent to existing land; capex and funding plan not finalised and will be discussed next quarter; phased, demand-linked investment.
Capacity utilisation is kept at roughly 70-75% by design; full-year production utilisation expected around 70%, with an enhancement plan this year.
Borrowings were about INR499 crore at 30 Sep 2026 after roughly INR490 crore of IPO proceeds were used for repayment in Q2.
demand_pricing: Order book at 30 Sep 2026 was about INR2,543 crore: manufacturing INR1,303 crore (about 85% cable, 15% conductor) and EPC INR1,240 crore.
Q2 order inflow about INR357 crore; H1 inflow about INR449 crore.
Manufacturing order book split is roughly 50:50 government and private; EPC customers are essentially all government, plus some private utilities.
Management says manufacturing cycles run about 6 months and EPC cycles 1.5-2 years.
Pricing: aluminium prices were stable in Q2 and most contracts are pass-through, so volume growth tracked revenue growth.
On competition, management argued that the newer-generation HTLS (TS Conductors licence) carries cost advantages that will hold against other licensees; no price-erosion data given.
Export opportunities are being examined for the longer term, with no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin upside from specialised products over 2-3 years, and can EBITDA margin reach 13-14%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said specialised products such as CLF and underground cabling are high-margin, and margin will improve as mix shifts. No numerical target beyond the 12.5-13% range was given.

qa_highlights.question: Project value, timeline and profitability of the CESC 220 kV underground order, and the government/private split?
qa_highlights.answer: The CESC order is about INR42-44 crore with a one-year execution timeline; EPC margins are expected at 14-16%. The manufacturing order book is about 50:50 government and private.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 EBITDA about INR340 crore on an implied INR2,700 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management repeated the 12.5-13% EBITDA margin guidance and said the H1 share of revenue is about 42%, without confirming the INR340 crore figure.

qa_highlights.question: Utilisation, volume growth and conductor-versus-cable mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year utilisation is around 70%. Volume growth matched revenue growth because of pass-through pricing. Cable should stay at 80-90% of manufacturing and conductor at 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was EPC revenue down about 51% and is the company deliberately shifting mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target mix is about 75:25 manufacturing to EPC, and the Q2 drop was due to heavy rain. About INR100 crore of EPC revenue was deferred.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital elevated and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose to INR946 crore from INR710 crore due to delays. Management said working capital peaked in September, is now normalising, and should fall 25-40 days by Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of the INR1,250 crore-plus order pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said further orders are expected by year-end, with inflows continuing each quarter. No specific pipeline figure was confirmed for H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why are segment margins moving the way they are?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the businesses are integrated and shared plants mean segment margins are not managed separately; it guides to overall EBITDA margin.

risks_watch: Working capital and cash conversion: inventory at INR946 crore and receivables at INR1,382 crore; operating cash flow was hit in Q2, and the FY27 positive-cash-flow target is unproven.
EPC execution risk from monsoon delays, with about INR100 crore of revenue deferred into Q2-Q3; EPC revenue fell about 51% YoY in Q2.

Order inflow of about INR357 crore in Q2 trailed Q2 revenue of INR628 crore, so the order book fell in absolute terms from the 30 Jun level; the analyst flagged slower order recognition than execution.
Competition from new HTLS licensees could pressure L1 pricing; management claims cost advantages but gave no evidence.
Kharagpur capex and funding are not yet finalised, and the timing and size of the investment are unclear.
Finance cost benefit from debt repayment is only partly visible in Q2 and should show fully in H2.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategic story (transmission entry, HTLS and 220 kV credentials), but cautious and sometimes vague on numbers: it deflected on segment margins, the Kharagpur capex and the FY27 EBITDA figure, and gave only qualitative answers on pricing and pipeline timing.
key_quotes: This is Laser's first commercial HTLS order. It marks the transition of our advanced conductor platform from development qualification to commercial execution.
So working capital is stretched because as I said that since our operations got delayed in EPC and which hampered our inventory.
Our approach will remain phased and disciplined. The timing and scale of investment will be aligned with demand visibility, product strategy, customer requirement and expected returns.

growth.why: Management guides only to a stable 12.5-13% EBITDA margin and ~INR100 crore of deferred EPC revenue recovery in Q2-Q3, with no explicit revenue growth figure; backing is an INR2,543 crore order book, but the Kharagpur plant has no capex, funding or timing yet and utilisation is held at ~70% by design.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin to stabilise at 12.5-13% (vs 12.1% in Q2 and 12.3% in H1), with mix shift to CLF and underground cabling cited but no target beyond that range.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation is held at about 70% by design and no new plant is commissioned in the window; the Kharagpur plant has no capex, funding or timing yet.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Manufacturing revenue grew 29.9% YoY in Q2 on a INR2,543 crore order book, and about INR100 crore of deferred EPC revenue is expected to be recovered in Q2-Q3, though Q2 order inflow of INR357 crore trailed revenue of INR628 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only about 70% and the WBIDC LoI for 40 acres at Kharagpur is in hand, but capex and funding are not finalised and management said they will be discussed next quarter.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the 12.5-13% margin range, did not confirm the analyst's INR340 crore FY27 EBITDA figure, and gave no revenue growth figure.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: EPC revenue fell about 51% YoY to INR104 crore in Q2, H1 EPC is down 10.7%, and FY27 EBITDA of INR340 crore was not confirmed, with the working capital and operating cash flow targets unproven.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The company has entered high-voltage transmission with a first HTLS order (INR72.76 crore from Power Grid) and a first 220 kV underground EPC order (about INR42-44 crore from CESC), but no dated launch was given.

rows.label: Working capital days down 25-40 by Q4 FY27
rows.why: Working capital is INR1,159 crore at 166 days, down from 183 days at end Q1, and management targets a 25-40 day cut by Q4 FY27, though inventory rose to INR946 crore.

rows.label: Lower interest cost after IPO-funded repayment
rows.why: Borrowings fell to about INR499 crore after about INR490 crore of IPO proceeds were used, and finance cost was INR33 crore in Q2 vs INR36 crore in Q1, with the full benefit expected in H2.

rows.label: Further order inflows by year-end
rows.why: Q2 inflow was about INR357 crore and H1 about INR449 crore against an INR2,543 crore order book, but management gave no firm H2 inflow figure.

oneOffs.what: About INR100 crore of EPC revenue deferred by monsoon delays out of Q2 into Q2-Q3, depressing Q2 YoY growth

quality.why: Q2 revenue grew only 2.1% YoY to INR628 crore: manufacturing rose 29.9% (INR404 to INR524 crore) and was volume-led with pass-through pricing, but EPC fell about 51% (INR212 to INR104 crore) because about INR100 crore was deferred by rain, which the brief presents as recoverable in Q2-Q3 rather than a permanent loss.
